pages.description: archipelago of Papua New Guinea
pages.extract:
Louisiade Archipelago is in Milne Bay in Papua New Guinea. It is
a beautiful, peaceful area in the south eastern tip of Papua New Guinea and is renowned for its beautiful coral reefs, a diver's paradise. Apart from passing yachties it receives very few tourists.

pages.title: Runcorn
pages.description: town and port in Cheshire, England, UK
pages.extract: The industrial inland port of Runcorn is a treasure trove of architectural styles, from medieval ruins to 1970s utopia. Its impressive bridges across the River Mersey mark the gateway north to cosmopolitan Liverpool and south to leafy Cheshire. Very much off the tourist trail, this town of 62,000 people (2021) nonetheless has some surprising hidden gems for curious urban explorers.

pages.extract: Tramore is a beach resort in County Waterford in Ireland - Trá Mhór in Irish is "big beach", referring to the 5-km spit across the bay. It's the county's second largest town, with a population in 2022 of more than 11,000.

pages.title: Acajutla
pages.description: district in Western Sonsonate, El Salvador
pages.extract: Acajutla is a small Pacific coast city in Western El Salvador. It is the main port for El Salvador, is a regionally important transportation hub, and is increasingly popular among tourists who come for the mellow vibe of the town and for the beautiful beaches known for calmer waters than most Pacific coast beaches in Central America.

pages.title: Mérens-les-Vals
pages.description: commune in Ariège, France
pages.extract: Mérens-les-Vals is a town in the Ariège department in France. Mérens-les-Vals is a stopover village on the GR 10 long-distance hiking trail. As a result, the town is the starting point for many hikes, such as the family-friendly Comte pond or the Bésines pond. The GR 10 leaves Ariège by crossing the Col de la Coume d'Agnel (2,470  m ).

pages.title: Alfonso Castañeda
pages.description: municipality of the Philippines in the province of Nueva Vizcaya
pages.extract: Alfonso Castañeda is a town in southern Nueva Vizcaya, Philippines. Situated at the headwaters of the Cagayan and Pampanga Rivers and the junction of two mountain ranges, it forms the lever in the pan-shaped province and has multiple natural attractions and indigenous tribes.
